hero.tag: Where will the fine particles be tomorrow, and the days after?
hero.lede: Every morning Otso takes the 00 UTC analysis of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service, the ECMWF weather forecast of the same hour and the fires seen by satellite, computes the transport of the air with FLEXGREEN and forecasts PM2.5 over all land, 12 hours to 5 days ahead, as an ensemble of 8 members. Otso is the coarse (0.4°) model of the Foehn paper, fine-tuned on the live inputs of 2026. The 1 km Foehn is not run in real time.
disc.title: Research forecast.
disc.long: Otso is an experiment of a university group, not an official service. It has not yet been evaluated in real time, it is not monitored around the clock, and it does not replace the air-quality forecasts, indices and alerts of your national or local authorities. If you must decide something about your health, use those.
disc.short: Not an official alert: for health decisions use your national air-quality service.
install.sub_desktop: Scan the code with your phone to open Otso there, then add it to your home screen:
install.sub_phone: Add Otso to your home screen:
install.sub_rest: nothing to download from a store, it opens full screen like an app, keeps the last forecast when you are offline and updates itself every morning.
install.ios_1: Scan the code, or open ammarkheder.com/Foehn/otso in Safari (not in another app's browser).
install.ios_2: Tap Share ⎙ (the square with an arrow, at the bottom).
install.ios_3: Scroll and choose Add to Home Screen, then Add.
install.ios_4: Otso is on your home screen and opens full screen; it keeps the last forecast when offline.
install.android_1: Scan the code, or open ammarkheder.com/Foehn/otso in Chrome.
install.android_2: Tap the Install Otso button below the code when it appears, or the ⋮ menu → Add to Home screen / Install app.
install.android_3: Confirm. Otso appears with the other apps.
install.desktop_2: Click the install icon at the right of the address bar, or menu → Install Otso (Firefox and Safari on Mac: keep it as a bookmark).
install.desktop_3: Otso opens in its own window.
install.note: Your city is remembered on this device only (nothing is sent anywhere). A new forecast appears each day around 12:30 UTC. Research forecast, not an alert: the app sends no notifications.
install.done: Otso is installed on this device. A new forecast appears each day around 12:30 UTC.
map.sub: Hover or tap a place for its value; click to keep it and see how it evolves over the five days. Scroll or pinch to zoom, drag to pan. Fields: the mean of the 8 members, their 90<sup>th</sup> percentile (a plausible bad case), and the share of members above 25 µg m<sup>−3</sup>, the limit of the "moderate" class of the European Air Quality Index for PM<sub>2.5</sub>.

city.note: Any city, town or village: 34,000 places above 15,000 inhabitants answer instantly (GeoNames, CC BY 4.0), the others come from OpenStreetMap as you type (© OpenStreetMap contributors). You can also click the map or use your position. The forecast is for the 0.4° cell (about 40 km) that contains the place.

cities.sub: Sixty large cities are published with every forecast; type any other city, town or village in the box to add it to the table (it is computed here from the forecast layers, and kept on this device). Values are the ensemble mean over the 3 × 3 cells around the place; the bars show the ten leads from +12 h to +120 h. Click a row to centre the map on it; sort by any column.
